thesis: Give an LLM multiple ways to observe an app, establish comparable measurements, preserve correctness and design, and verify optimizations with evidence.

concepts.name: The website test bench
concepts.prompt: A physical website made of thick white layered paper, standing upright as a browser window with a top bar, three tiny circular controls and a grid of rectangular picture cards. It is clamped in a precision testing jig on a modern olive-green laboratory bench. A real steel caliper measures the spacing of its cards; a small camera lens points at the page; attached signal leads connect the jig to one compact central instrument controller with a paper strip showing unlabeled block-shaped profiling traces. Make the connections orderly and purposeful. Central page and caliper dominate, camera and controller secondary; this is a coherent instrumented test, not a collection of floating icons. Editorial object photography with paper sculpture, cool mint and brushed silver, punchy tangerine accents, clean daylight, close frontal three-quarter view. Avoid antique steampunk machinery. Wide landscape 16:9 editorial hero for DanLevy.net, mature Paper atelier visual language, intelligent tactile independent technical journal. Topic: connect an LLM agent to multiple real measurement tools for a website—browser profiling, screenshots, session recordings, accessibility audits and repeatable benchmarks—then optimize against evidence, not guesses. A website must be recognizable through physical browser-window geometry and page layout blocks, never a generic laptop as the whole idea. No words, letters, numbers, logos, watermarks, invented benchmark values, robot heads, glowing brains, holograms, corporate 3D blobs. Measurement marks without numerals are allowed. No floating unrelated symbols. Strong focal hierarchy and central crop-safe composition for 2.25:1; all essential objects have breathing room.
concepts.squareNotes: Keep browser specimen, caliper, camera and controller compact.

concepts.name: The evidence light table
concepts.prompt: Top-down art-directed photographic collage of a real luminous editor's light table: a large translucent browser-page proof in the center, with three clearly different evidence strips aligned directly against its edges: a contact sheet of the same page at successive moments (screen recording), a densely layered amber block trace (profiler), and a transparent overlay of keyboard-focus outlines joined in reading order (accessibility). The screenshot is the central specimen these instruments examine. A precise steel measuring rule with fine tick marks but no numerals crosses two page proofs to compare unchanged geometry. One narrow cable connects a small matte-black controller to the table at the bottom. Rich midnight blue around luminous frosted white, amber and restrained coral, physical acetate, photographic film perforations and torn-paper edges. Sophisticated dense-but-ordered editorial flat lay; purposeful evidence, not decorative charts. No hands. concepts.name: The browser wind tunnel
concepts.prompt: An expansive environmental editorial scene inside a daylight engineering test laboratory. A large sculptural browser webpage built from layered paper sits inside a transparent rectangular wind-tunnel test chamber. Thin parallel physical white airflow filaments run across the page, bunching visibly at one oversized raised orange image tile, exposing a bottleneck. A mounted small high-speed camera observes that tile, two sensor probes touch the specimen, their cables run visibly to a single modest measurement console beside the chamber. The browser page must be unmistakable and dominate; the transparent chamber explains controlled testing and repeated measurement. Mix cut photographic collage and finely crafted paper with real environmental depth, pale sky blue glass, rust-orange page tile, charcoal support structure, sunny natural shadows. Not sci-fi, not a car, not a miniature beige machine product shot. concepts.name: Many lenses, one page
concepts.prompt: Bold sculptural editorial paper-and-optics composition: one oversized white browser-window paper cutout lies on deep cobalt textured paper. Three distinct physical optical inspection lenses are mounted together on one brushed metal arm above the same page, each lens exposing a different layer of that single page: its visual card layout, its layered warm-orange profiling blocks, and its precise green keyboard-focus path around the same buttons. All lenses are visibly joined to ONE inspection apparatus with one cable exiting toward a small plain controller. Tight macro view, strong three-circle rhythm, real glass refraction and interlayer shadows, crisp cut-paper forms, cobalt white orange and emerald. No magnifying-glass handles, no loose orbiting icons. Make this a striking simple editorial emblem for giving an agent several kinds of sight, legible at 200 pixels. concepts.name: Make the improvement measurable
concepts.prompt: High-end mixed-media editorial print and photographic collage, straight-on wide composition. Two nearly identical browser-page paper specimens are mounted side by side on one shared precise calibration grid with subtle unnumbered tick marks. Their content card arrangement and visual design match exactly. Below the left page is a thick stack of red-orange horizontal paper strips representing work consumed; below the right is a visibly shorter stack of teal strips, both measured from the SAME baseline by a steel caliper spanning the comparison. A photographic film strip showing the matching page frames bridges the two specimens along the top, indicating visual correctness is preserved. One small black probe touching each stack connects to a single compact cream measurement instrument between them. Focus on comparable measurement plus unchanged app, no victory badges or magic speed icons. Warm chalk, vermilion, teal, black ink, rough screenprint textures and crisp photographic steel; graphic restrained publication cover, not an infographic or dashboard.
